name: SS blood group tattoo
subcategory: German WWII tattoos indicating blood type
summary: SS blood group tattoos (German: Blutgruppentätowierung) were worn by members of the SS-Verfügungstruppe, SS-Totenkopfverbände, and most of the Waffen-SS in Nazi Germany during World War II to identify the individual's blood type.
description: SS blood group tattoos (German: Blutgruppentätowierung) were worn by members of the SS-Verfügungstruppe, SS-Totenkopfverbände, and most of the Waffen-SS in Nazi Germany during World War II to identify the individual's blood type. After the war, the tattoo was taken to be prima facie evidence of being part of the Waffen-SS, leading to potential arrest and prosecution.
